intended_object: The constant "angular direction" vector field `(0,1)` on the library's own chart space `Absolute := AbsolutePoint × ℝ`. It is one of the frame directions (radial, axial, angular, fast) fed into `CurlClassBounds.realizedCoefficient` and `phaseNormal`. I inferred this from the docstring, the name and how the file uses it.
explanation: The body is a constant function that ignores its argument and returns the unit vector of the last `ℝ` factor in `AbsolutePoint × ℝ`. `Absolute` is a product type made up for this one Navier–Stokes construction, out of `PhaseCalculus.Slow × TorusInverse.Plane` and `ℝ`. The definition only names the angular coordinate direction in that chart, so the proof can use it alongside `absoluteRadial`, `absoluteAxial` and `absoluteFast`. No standard notion in the literature corresponds to it; it is an internal device of this proof.
